restrictions: Two distinct 64-byte messages with equal digests for the Orchard hash with 9 partial rounds (poseidon-orchard-r9-prefix-v1), found as a collision F(x) = F(y), x != y, of the walk F(x) = digest(message(x + rho0)) / OUTSCALE: message() is the injective parametrisation of the input line on which rounds 0 and 1 are affine, OUTSCALE a fixed nonzero field constant, rho0 a random 254-bit coin of the attempt. Plain birthday search, one trail with distinguished points, one table; the success probability uses no property of the rounds.

Cost model orchard-field-ram-v2, C = 405. Prices used: canonical field ADD and MUL 1/C each; every other primitive 256-bit word operation (AND, OR, shift, compare, branch, register move, aligned load or store, random word) 1/C. No permutation call is charged as a unit: every evaluation executes the 248-operation step program (97 ADD, 151 MUL; proof.md Section 2, listing in Appendix C), an equivalent form of rounds 2-63 that equals the reference digest divided by OUTSCALE. Constant loads: the 94 step constants are loaded once per attempt (94 loads, charged) into a declared file of 155 256-bit registers, counted in memory; arithmetic takes register operands.

Ledger (proof.md Section 6, instruction listings): a trail step is 248 + 3 operations, plus 3 per block of 4 unrolled steps; a recovery evaluation at most 248 + 6; table scan, insertion, bisection, constant loads, the message roots and setup are at most 15,442,595,772 operations. The offline derivation of the step constants and fixed parameters (build_step, tune.py in exact integer arithmetic, one run of plan) is bounded by 186,965,847,824 word operations from the metered counts of the shipped code (proof.md Section 6a, Appendix G); that bound is inside time_log2 and is also declared as preprocessing_log2 = 29 (one quantity, not added twice). time_log2 is the full budget with every halt charged at its limit: S = n + d trail steps and 3 gmax recovery evaluations, log2 T = 126.795509, claimed 126.79551 (rounded up). One attempt; no restart, amplification or advice.

Memory: 28,509 table entries of one 32-byte word (high 126 bits of the value OR index), a side array of 16-bit low parts (1,782 words), the start word, code at most 1,969 instructions at 36 bytes, constants and the 155-register file: 1,048,548 bytes, below 2^20 (proof.md Section 7; the code term and the word layout are derived there).

Success probability at least 0.39: Lemma 2 (proof.md Section 5) proves 0.62000000305122585231 (at least 0.62) for a uniformly random function at the filed budget, and 0.39 at a budget 1.3992 times smaller (0.4846 bit of the claimed time), with explicit terms for the trail, detection, table and gaps. H1 (the only premise, score-critical, an assumption, no proof is known) states that the real map with the random coin rho0 reaches 0.39 at the filed budget; measurements of the real map family at r = 7, 23 and 56 on truncated outputs are in proof.md Section 8.

The program is printed in full in proof.md Appendix B (standard library only); the step program in Appendix C. One organizer-run experiment is declared (linewalk-10bit, python-message-pairs-v1, event digest-xor-mask; source experiments/exp_row.py): the attempt's own line map and walk at 10 bits, at this row's round count, returning the colliding pair of the walk; a reduced event that witnesses nothing about full width, cost or the success probability (proof.md Section 9). Participant measurements: replay sources in Appendix D, data in Appendix E, per-job seeds and records in Appendix F. No full collision is produced or claimed; the claim is the cost of the search.

heuristics.statement: Let n0 = 133586732 * 2^100 be the number of trail steps at which the Lemma 2 bound for a uniformly random function is 0.39. The filed trail has n = 186919966 * 2^100 = 1.3992 n0 steps (0.4846 bit more time), at which Lemma 2 gives 0.620000003 for a uniformly random function. Premise: for the attempt's coins rho0 and x_0 (uniform 254-bit words), the search of proof.md Section 3 on the real map F(x) = digest(message(x + rho0)) / OUTSCALE, at the budget n, succeeds with probability at least 0.39. This is an assumption; no proof is known.
heuristics.scope: Target poseidon-orchard-r9-prefix-v1, inputs on the line of proof.md Section 1, one trail with the parameters of proof.md Section 3 (S = 2.370e38 evaluations). Not claimed for other round counts or budgets. Only the success probability rests on it; the step program, the recovery, the ledger and the memory are proved or checked exactly (proof.md Sections 2, 4, 6, 7).
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer-run experiment linewalk-10bit (python-message-pairs-v1, digest-xor-mask, 256 trials; proof.md Section 9): regime = the attempt's own line map message() and walk, at this row's round count r = 9, with the leading 10 bits of the digest as the walk value, run to its first repeat (about 40 evaluations for a random function on 1,024 points), the colliding pair returned and its digests checked by the organizer; it witnesses that the line map, the r-round digest and the pair extraction work at one reduced width, and the runner infers no probability. Sensitivity of that experiment: none to the collision rate (every function on 1,024 values repeats within 1,025 evaluations, so every trial returns a pair); the margin down to c = 0.511 rests on the participant measurements. Participant measurements (not organizer-run; per-job seeds, records and counts in proof.md Appendix F) on the real map family at r = 7, 23 and 56 partial rounds with outputs truncated to w = 16..40 bits (F_w(v) = low w bits of F(v), a fresh rho and start per trial, as in the attempt), 20,616 walks: the hazard multiplier (collision rate relative to a random function, estimated from the exact discrete first-repeat law, profile-likelihood interval, coverage checked by simulation in proof.md Section 8) is 1.001, 95% interval [0.987, 1.015], with slope -0.0011 per bit (standard error 0.0015) across widths; the full search succeeded in 3,463/8,616 = 0.402 runs at widths 24..40 against a mean Lemma 2 bound of 0.3900; DP gaps follow the geometric law and stayed below gmax. Extrapolation from these widths to 254 bits and 2^127 steps, and to r = 9, is by this premise. Sensitivity: if the real map has the collision rate of a random function times a factor c, success is about 1 - exp(-c x) - n/N - eps with x = 0.96975; it stays at least 0.39 for every c >= 0.511 (a deficit of up to 48.9 percent); c = 1, 0.9, 0.75, 0.6, 0.5, 0.4 give the values in the table of proof.md Section 8.
heuristics.limitations: The organizer experiment is one width (10 bits), this row's round count and a witness-only event on the digest of the line walk G, not on the scaled walk map F at full width; it cannot measure the collision rate. The participant measurements reach outputs of at most 40 bits and trails of at most 2,970,429 steps, at three round counts; they show the random-function collision law of the real round function at these widths and do not bound the collision rate at 254 bits. On a single fixed map the success over starts varies with that map's longest cycle; the attempt therefore draws rho0, and H1 concerns the average over rho0.
